data.narrative:
NVision Imaging Technologies is a Series A stage biotech company founded by Plenio, Schwartz, Jelezko, Retzker, and Brosh, having raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private comparables including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given available data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $20M total raised as a baseline, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent funding rounds, yielding a $40M implied valuation. This method is defensible for early-stage funding-based assessment but relies on historical stage progression norms rather than company-specific fundamentals.

Peer-median triangulation was not feasible: while 7 same-sector peers exist in Biotech & Health, none of the narrower filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comps) produced the minimum 3 datapoints required for reliable statistical anchoring. Public-comp valuation proved inapplicable due to the absence of revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. The analysis therefore supports a valuation range of $34M–$46M, centered at $40M, with critical uncertainty around the target's revenue trajectory, patent position, and pathway to clinical or commercial inflection. A narrower range would require revenue data or closer-stage peer comparables.
